title: Playing the introduction on a Buck and Bubbles record
summary: He was called to the studio to play an introduction to Turn Back the Clock that trumpeters could not read.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And I also did some recording, Bucking 2nd Bubbles, you know about that?
Well of course, I didn't know that you were -- what did you do with Bucking 2nd Bubbles?
Well, called me from the studio one day and said, they were recording and they said -- they sent for me to come up to the recording studio and I think, Bill Solomon Gomo was up there.

Yeah, he was in that -- made that session. They were having some trouble with getting the trumpet player to play the introduction, Bud Johnson was the contractor for the band. And he wrote something that the trumpet players couldn't play. So they sent for me to come up there just to play the introduction. I think the tune was "Turn Back the Clock," so I went up there and I played the introduction and that was all. I could go on back to the studio.
That's allyou did, just play the introduction?
Yeah, because you know being a lead
man for so long, those things are very easy for me.
And it was very hard -- difficult for a jazz man to play something like that Bud had written. So I went up there and played the introduction and I came on back to the studio.
